title: Feature flagging + progressive rollout guardrails for hot-route capacity protection
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Problem
We need a reversible, low-risk way to enable hot-route capacity protection (tier-aware quotas/rate limits + priority admission control) region-by-region and account-by-account. Without strong guardrails, we risk:
- enabling protection globally with incorrect thresholds (sudden 429 spikes for enterprise)
- partial rollout where gateway/routing/runtime disagree on enforcement (hard-to-debug behavior)
- inability to quickly rollback during incidents

Scope
Add feature flags and rollout controls with safe defaults + rollback hooks:
1) Region gating: enablement by region (e.g., us-east canary -> eu-west -> full).
2) Account allowlist gating: allowlist enterprise accounts/routes for early canary.
3) Route group gating: only enforce on explicitly protected route groups (e.g., chat/completions, embeddings, rerank), default off.
4) Safe defaults: protection OFF unless explicitly enabled. For enabled regions, deny enabling for routes not in protected set.
5) Rollback hooks: one-command rollback (disable flags, revert config snapshot, and force policy cache invalidation).
6) Consistency checks: preflight validation that config migrations, policy schema versions, and runtime metric exports are present for the target region.

Non-goals
- New billing behavior. We only tag/emit metadata for throttling decisions.
- Customer-specific “dynamic pricing” or fairness-scheduler rewrite.

Proposed flag model
We will use a hierarchical rollout model evaluated in control plane and mirrored into gateway + routing via config push:
- hot_route_protection.enabled (global master switch; default false)
- hot_route_protection.regions_enabled (comma-separated region list; empty by default)
- hot_route_protection.account_allowlist (list of account IDs; empty by default)
- hot_route_protection.route_groups_enabled (list; empty by default)
- hot_route_protection.mode ("observe" | "enforce"; default "observe" for first enablement)
- hot_route_protection.rollback_token (string; changes trigger immediate cache bust across policy evaluators)

Evaluation semantics (must be deterministic + auditable)
- If master switch is false => behave exactly as today (no new throttling path, no new 429 reason codes).
- If enabled but region not in regions_enabled => no-op.
- If region enabled but route_group not enabled => no-op.
- If route_group enabled but account not allowlisted:
  - For enterprise tier: no-op until GA phase (explicitly controlled by a separate "enterprise_default_on" flag; default false).
  - For best-effort tier: allow controlled throttling only after SRE sign-off (we keep best-effort behind allowlist for first canary to avoid surprises during game day tooling shakeout).
- mode=observe => compute decisions + emit metrics/reason codes internally but do not shed/throttle; still return 200/normal behavior.
- mode=enforce => apply admission control + tier-aware 429 behavior.

Guardrails
- Config preflight: refuse to enable enforce mode for a region unless runtime queue depth + scheduler lag metrics are present in the last 10 minutes (prevents “flying blind”).
- Version pinning: policy schema version must be >= priority-class schema (ENG-4923). Gateway config must include route-group mapping (ENG-4922). Routing build must include capacity-signal admission control (ENG-4924).
- Blast radius controls: max allowlist size in canary mode (e.g., 20 accounts) unless override requires explicit approvals from SRE lead + product.
- Rollback: region disablement takes precedence over all other flags. Also support an emergency “enforcement_kill_switch” that bypasses policy evaluation entirely to reduce latency overhead under incident.

Acceptance criteria
- Can enable in us-east for 1-3 allowlisted enterprise accounts and only 1 route group (chat/completions) with mode=observe, verify:
  - decision logging works
  - metrics emitted with correct tier attribution
  - no behavior change for customers
- Switch to mode=enforce for allowlisted accounts in us-east with measurable effect:
  - best-effort sheds before enterprise under induced pressure
  - enterprise p95/p99 stays within SLO targets during game day
- Rollback executed successfully within 5 minutes:
  - enforcement stops
  - caches invalidated (no lingering “enforce” decisions)
  - incident-bot notification posted (ENG-4927)
- Auditability:
  - on-call can query which flag state applied for a specific request (via decision log + admin debug endpoint once available)

Implementation plan (high level)
1) Control plane: define flag schema + propagation to gateway/routing config bundles.
2) Gateway: read rollout config, attach evaluation context (region, account_id, route_group, tier) to policy eval call.
3) Policy engine: treat flags as first-class inputs and log decision rationale ("flag_disabled", "region_disabled", "account_not_allowlisted", etc.).
4) Routing: only enforce admission control when enforce mode is active and route/account/tier match.
5) Tooling: rollout CLI script + runbook section for enable/disable + snapshotting.

Links
- Epic: ENG-4921
- Related:
  - ENG-4922 API gateway tier-aware rate limiter
  - ENG-4923 Policy engine priority class evaluation
  - ENG-4924 Routing integrate capacity signals
  - ENG-4925 Runtime export queue depth + scheduler lag
- Rollout PR (expected): sources/github/redwood/pr-27452-enable-feature-flagged-hot-route-protection-us-east-canary.json
- Launch checklist: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/launch-checklist-hot-route-capacity-protection.json

Risks / open questions
- Account ID allowlist location: do we key by internal tenant_id vs external org_id? Decision: use tenant_id as primary, with mapping tooling for Support/CS.
- Flag evaluation overhead: ensure no per-request remote calls; all flags must be in local config bundle with periodic refresh.
- Security: admin rollback endpoints and debug endpoints must be restricted and audited.

Owner(s)
- Benji Okafor (Control plane rollout primitives)
- Amara Diallo (Gateway wiring)
- Mina Haddad / Elena Popov (Routing gating)
- Rafael Mendes (SRE go/no-go + rollback playbook)

Definition of Done
- All flags available in config, tested in staging + us-east canary
- Documented enablement/rollback steps in runbook + launch checklist
- Alerts and incident-bot notifications integrated for “protection active” and “rollback performed” events
comments: 2025-12-07 (Benji Okafor): Drafted flag schema proposal. Strong preference for config-bundle based flags (no online eval) to avoid adding latency/jitter to gateway. Will add a kill-switch that bypasses policy evaluation entirely for incident scenarios.

2025-12-09 (Ravi Menon): Please ensure flag gates are applied consistently across gateway + routing. We can’t have routing enforcing when gateway thinks it’s observe-only (or vice versa). Suggest adding a shared “enforcement_epoch” token so all components converge quickly after changes.

2025-12-11 (Jordan Lee): From policy engine POV: flags should be included as inputs to the decision record, with explicit “deny reason” when policy would have shed but flag prevented enforcement. This will make canary observe-mode useful for tuning thresholds.

2025-12-13 (Rafael Mendes): SRE requirement: enforce-mode enablement must fail closed if we don’t see queue depth + scheduler lag metrics in-region. Also need a 1-command rollback that invalidates caches; prior incidents showed stale policy caches lasting ~15m if we just flip config.

2025-12-16 (Amara Diallo): Gateway wiring in progress. Route-group mapping is the tricky part; we’ll treat /v1/chat/completions and /v1/embeddings as explicit groups; default group = “unprotected” to avoid accidental coverage.

2026-01-06 (Benji Okafor): Implemented rollout CLI script: enable-region, disable-region, set-mode observe/enforce, update allowlist, bump rollback_token (forces cache bust). Added guardrail: allowlist size capped unless “--override” with approver notes logged.

2026-01-14 (Aisha Bello): Verified staging: observe mode emits metrics without behavior change. Confirmed region disablement overrides everything. Added runbook snippet for checking current state and for validating metrics presence before enable.

2026-01-22 (Rafael Mendes): us-east canary readiness: go/no-go checklist complete. We will start with 2 enterprise accounts + chat route group in observe for 30 minutes, then enforce for 15 minutes during controlled load injection.

2026-01-29 (Talia Benson): Marking Done. Guardrails in place; rollout path used successfully in canary and EU follow-on. Follow-up: ensure Support tooling can translate customer org -> tenant_id quickly (tracked in ENG-4930).
